function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
Below are some common ways to pull **detailed information** (speed, duplex, MAC address, driver, firmware, statistics, etc.) for a network interface on different platforms.  
Pick the one that matches your operating system / environment and let me know if you need help tailoring it to a particular device or script.

---

## 1️⃣ Linux / Unix‑like systems  

| Tool | What it shows | Typical usage |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| `ip link show <iface>` | Interface state, MTU, flags, MAC address, driver name, speed/duplex (if supported) | `ip link show eth0` |
| `ethtool <iface>` | Driver version, firmware, supported speeds, current speed/duplex, link status, statistics counters | `ethtool eth0` |
| `ethtool -S <iface>` | Raw statistics counters (bytes, packets, errors, collisions, etc.) | `ethtool -S eth0` |
| `ethtool -i <iface>` | Driver/module information (driver name, version, firmware, bus info) | `ethtool -i eth0` |
| `ethtool -m <iface>` | EEPROM contents (useful for checking firmware revision) | `ethtool -m eth0` |
| `cat /sys/class/net/<iface>/statistics/*` | Individual counter files (rx_bytes, tx_packets, rx_errors, …) | `cat /sys/class/net/eth0/statistics/rx_bytes` |
| `lshw -class network -short` | Hardware description (model, vendor, serial, config) | `sudo lshw -class network -short` |
| `dmidecode -t 2` | BIOS/SMBIOS information (may contain NIC serial numbers) | `sudo dmidecode -t 2` |

### Example: Get all details for `eth0`

```bash
# Basic interface info
ip link show eth0

# Driver & firmware
ethtool -i eth0

# Current operational settings
ethtool eth0

# Statistics
ethtool -S eth0

# Raw EEPROM (firmware)
ethtool -m eth0
```

---

## 2️⃣ macOS  

| Command | What it shows | Usage |
|---------|---------------|-------|
| `networksetup -getinfo <service>` | Service name, IP, subnet mask, router, DNS servers | `networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi` |
| `ifconfig <iface>` | Flags, MAC, MTU, link status, raw statistics | `ifconfig en0` |
| `netstat -I <iface> -b` | Bytes transmitted/received, packet counts | `netstat -I en0 -b` |
| `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType` | Full hardware + software details | `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType` |

---

## 3️⃣ Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
# Basic adapter properties
Get-NetAdapter -Name "<adapter>" | Format-List *

# Detailed stats
Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name "<adapter>"

# Driver info
Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name "<adapter>" | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -eq "Driver Version"}

# Link speed
(Get-NetAdapter -Name "<adapter>").LinkSpeed

# Physical location (slot, port)
Get-NetAdapter -Name "<adapter>" | Select-Object Name, Location
```

*Example:*  

```powershell
Get-NetAdapter -Name "Ethernet" | Format-List *
Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name "Ethernet"
```

---

## 4️⃣ Using SNMP (works on most managed devices)

```bash
# Basic interface description
snmpwalk -v2c -c public <device_ip> IF-MIB::ifDescr

# Speed (in bits per second)
snmpwalk -v2c -c public <device_ip> IF-MIB::ifSpeed

# Status
snmpwalk -v2c -c public <device_ip> IF-MIB::ifOperStatus

# Statistics
snmpwalk -v2c -c public <device_ip> IF-MIB::ifInOctets
snmpwalk -v2c -c public <device_ip> IF-MIB::ifOutOctets
```

Replace `<device_ip>` with the target host’s IP and adjust community string (`public`) as needed.

---

## 5️⃣ Using REST APIs (for modern SDN controllers or cloud providers)

Many SDN controllers expose a REST endpoint such as:

```
GET https://<controller>/api/v1/interfaces/<id>
```

Typical response fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `id` | Interface identifier |
| `name` | Human‑readable name |
| `macAddress` | MAC address |
| `linkSpeed` | Current negotiated speed |
| `duplex` | Duplex mode |
| `status` | Operational status (up/down) |
| `statistics` | Dictionary of counters (rxBytes, txPackets, …) |
| `driver` | Driver name & version |
| `firmware` | Firmware revision |

Use `curl` or a programming language library to hit the endpoint and parse the JSON.

---

## Quick Checklist for “Detailed Information”

1. **Hardware ID** – MAC address, serial number, PCI slot.  
2. **Driver & Firmware** – Driver module, firmware revision, driver version.  
3. **Operational State** – Link status, speed, duplex, auto‑negotiation.  
4. **Statistics** – Packets, bytes, errors, collisions, dropped frames.  
5. **Configuration** – MTU, VLAN tags, QoS settings, ACLs.  
6. **Physical Location** – Slot, port, rack position (if available).  

If you’re scripting this, consider wrapping the above commands into a shell script or PowerShell function so you can pass an interface name and get a unified report.

Let me know which platform you’re targeting or if you’d like a sample script that aggregates all of the above!
